result:
Parking the roadmap. This closes the open O2 question: nothing gets promoted, and no stage is handed off.

**What parks:** Stage 2 (closure notices, Track B) and Track A's Ranked list (O2, O3, O4). That is four deferred items, one each. Stage 1 stays complete, and its findings file stays where it is. This roadmap has no spec, so there are no methodology or critique files to retire.

First I need the deferred-item schema and the current backlog:

```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/references/deferred-backlog.md
Read specs/deferred_items.md        # may not exist yet
```

Then I'll append this section, adjusted to match the schema's exact fields once I've read it:

```markdown
## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06

- [ ] Closure notices to boat operators (was Stage 2, Track B)
      Context: email boat operators within an hour of a lock closing, by polling the closure log about every 10 minutes. Parked when the canal study's funding ended.
      Size: small
      Done when: the notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and in a test an email reaches every address on the list within an hour of a new closure entry.

- [ ] 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock (was O2, Track A rank 1)
      Context: Stage 1 found that closure chance is under 2% of days below a gauge level of 3.1 m and rises to about 60% at 3.8 m (specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md). Its one fit took 22 min on 1.8 GB. Drive that curve from the river-level forecast, one run a day.
      Size: small
      Done when: a 7-day closure-risk outlook for each lock is produced from the river-level forecast.

- [ ] Pooled per-lock closure curves for all 14 locks (was O3, Track A rank 2)
      Context: Stage 1's four longest-record locks showed close to the same curve (findings file above). Expect about 14 times Stage 1's data, roughly 25 GB.
      Size: medium
      Done when: separate closure curves for all 14 locks, pooled across locks, are fit on the real data.

- [ ] Closure-history map for boat operators (was O4, Track A rank 3)
      Context: one static map page of each lock's closure history.
      Size: about a day
      Done when: a closure-history map for the canal's boat operators is published.
```

Then I'll retire the roadmap and commit on `main`:

```
git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
# add under the title:  > PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete
git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap: 1 of 2 stages complete; remaining work to deferred_items"
```

Once that's committed, the roadmap is closed. The four items will age in `specs/deferred_items.md` like any other deferred work. The closure-notices item is there too: you could pick it up on its own later, because it doesn't depend on the curve.
